html:
The departure of the Ewe peoples from Notse, a walled town in southern Togo, which tradition places in the 17th or early 18th century, when they fled the harsh king Agokoli.

The story says the people loosened a section of the town wall by throwing water on it, then walked out backwards so their footprints seemed to lead in. They spread west across the Volta into today's Ghana and south to the coast, founding many small chiefdoms. Notse's walls still stand in part, and the Agbogbo-za festival recalls the exodus. The Ewe were later split by the borders of German Togoland and the British Gold Coast, a divide that lasts.
sum: The departure of the Ewe peoples from Notse, a walled town in southern Togo, which tradition places in the 17th or early 18th century, when they fled the harsh king Agokoli.
